title: The Last Yearbook
premise: Paloma Almeida, senior debate captain at Marigold Prep, has perfected the art of the polished non-answer — until a college essay prompt ('What is the truest thing you've never said?') leaks into the school's anonymous confession app and starts exposing everyone's secrets, including her own. As the confessions unravel friendships and threaten her scholarship hopes, Paloma must choose between protecting her best friend's secret, her mother's fragile reputation, and the truth about why her father really left. To survive the year, she has to win the state championship she no longer believes in — and lose the argument that keeps her silent — before prom night forces every hidden thing into the open. In the end, Paloma publishes the yearbook with one page left unedited: the honest answers, including hers.
about_author: J. M. Crane is the pen name of a former high-school debate coach who spent six years watching teenagers say brilliant things they didn't mean. They write from a small apartment full of trophies they can't remember winning.

chapters.title: The Art of the Non-Answer
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She wins a practice debate on a topic she doesn't believe in, then comes home to a dinner-table argument about college money she deliberately loses by going quiet. Establishes her two voices: champion outside, silence inside. Emotional beat: competent numbness masking dread.

chapters.title: Prompt 4
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. English teacher Ms. Okafor assigns a college essay: 'What is the truest thing you've never said?' Paloma writes something devastatingly honest, then shreds it — but her lab partner Dev photographs it as a joke. Beat: the first crack in the wall.

chapters.title: Marigold Confesses
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The essay prompt goes viral on the school's anonymous app; confessions flood in overnight — cheating scandals, crushes, betrayals. Dev realizes he caused it and tells no one. Beat: giddy chaos curdling into guilt.

chapters.title: Captain's Privilege
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A confession implicates her co-captain Theo in leaking last year's case files to a rival school. Principal Voss pressures Paloma to identify the poster or forfeit their championship eligibility. Beat: loyalty vs. duty begins its squeeze.

chapters.title: What Theo Knew
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo admits privately he leaked the files to pay off a debt to a tutor ring — but begs Paloma to stay silent because his scholarship is his family's only exit. Beat: love against duty, first weight.

chapters.title: The Mother Question
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A confession hints that Paloma's mother, the school nurse, covered up an injury scandal years ago. Paloma confronts her mother, who deflects with practiced calm — the same skill Paloma inherited. Beat: the home argument she always loses.

chapters.title: Debate Camp for Liars
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The team preps for regionals while the app burns hotter; teammates start accusing each other mid-practice. Dev, still hiding his role, coaches Paloma through a speech about honesty that makes her flinch. Beat: irony sharpening into pain.

chapters.title: Regionals
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. They win regionals on a technicality, not merit, and Paloma feels nothing. Voss publicly praises the team while privately threatening expulsion over the app. Beat: hollow victory.

chapters.title: The Page Nobody Wrote
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. As yearbook editor, Paloma discovers a sealed 1999 page — the year her father left — hidden by a previous editor. It references 'the nurse's office.' Beat: the past reaching into the present.

chapters.title: Promises in the Archive
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo helps Paloma dig into the archive; they find her mother's name redacted across three documents. Growing closeness between them turns almost-romantic, then Theo pulls away, ashamed of what he's asked her to carry. Beat: tenderness interrupted.

chapters.title: Leak
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The app is traced to Dev's laptop. Voss suspends him pending expulsion, and Dev, cornered, implies Paloma knew. Beat: betrayal born of panic, not malice.

chapters.title: The Argument at Home
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma finally says the truest thing out loud — that she's been managing everyone's silences since her father left — and her mother slaps the table and admits the cover-up was to protect Paloma's father, not herself. Beat: the dam cracks.

chapters.title: Suspended
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Voss suspends Paloma too, citing 'guilt by association,' jeopardizing her scholarship. The team must choose: defend her or compete without her. Beat: isolation at the worst moment.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo confesses publicly to the leak to clear Paloma, sacrificing his own scholarship chances. Paloma is furious — he stole her choice — and says so. Beat: love and duty collide head-on.

chapters.title: Reinstated, Conditionally
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Voss offers reinstatement if Paloma delivers a scripted statement blaming Dev alone. Paloma accepts the deal — and hates herself for it. Beat: power corrupting someone good.

chapters.title: State Semifinals
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Back on the team, Paloma debates flawlessly while Dev watches her become everything she despises. He leaves an anonymous confession naming himself again — this time taking full blame. Beat: redemption attempted quietly.

chapters.title: The Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. On stage at the state final, mid-round, Paloma abandons her prepared case and argues the truest thing instead — losing the match on purpose. The gym goes silent. Beat: the climax of principle over prize.

chapters.title: Prom Night
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. At prom, Voss moves to expel Paloma and Dev; students rise one by one reading their own confessions aloud until the room sides with them. Theo takes Paloma's hand in front of everyone. Beat: collective courage, romantic payoff.

chapters.title: Voss Falls
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The unsealed 1999 page surfaces publicly; Voss resigns rather than face the board. Paloma feels no triumph — only the strange lightness of having nothing left to hide. Beat: power's corruption answered, not avenged.

chapters.title: The One That Does
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. With the season dead, the team stages an unofficial exhibition debate — open topics, real answers — packing the auditorium. Paloma and Theo argue opposite sides of loyalty vs. truth and both win. Beat: joy rebuilt on honesty.

chapters.title: Yearbook Deadline
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Printing deadline midnight: Paloma adds a final unedited page — the essay prompt and her answer, signed. Her mother reads it before anyone else and, for once, doesn't argue back. Beat: reconciliation without erasure.

chapters.title: Signed, Paloma Almeida
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, epilogue. Graduation; the yearbook circulates with her page dog-eared by dozens of hands. Dev heads to a coding program, Theo to a state school nearby, and Paloma submits her real essay — the shredded one, retyped — to her dream college. Final beat: visible at last, and fine. Actually fine.
